annotations.coverageReview: Visible front and side survey images and corrected four-patch overlays inspected. Storm Lion upper cheek, nose, lower mouth and side jaw are covered. The initial lower pick hit the beard and was replaced with the lower mouth. Mane, scarf, tail and legs still require complete animation review.

review.name: Storm Lion
findings: All 13 source clips actually inspected in 12 enlarged face/body front/side slices. Clear lower-mouth collapse during early recoil (12.5%) and lower jaw/cheek shear in strike and turned defeat. Mane, scarf and tail require preservation. Raw forelegs fold forward during strike/recoil; actual technique and planted-paw coordination specifically remain open. The corresponding battle face/body slices were also actually inspected; the same facial problem is present and there are no additional detached body surfaces in these raw clips. Equipped-technique review remains open.

companionTechniqueAudit.finding: All 36 final rebuilt battle technique sheets actually inspected. The torso, knees and support paws remain coordinated, toes no longer disappear through the floor, and the moving front paw returns coherently to stance. Face and mane remain intact.

sourceVisualFirstPass.finding: All 12 V4 source candidate face/body slices actually inspected. V1 beard strips and V3 chest stretching were rejected visually despite numerical passes. V4 keeps the lower beard extent with conservative forward/lateral limits; turned defeat and victory show a coherent beard, scarf and chest. Existing generic strike/recoil foreleg reach requires separate actual equipped-technique review.

supportedActionCandidate.required: All nine source-candidate techniques, enlarged all-clip source capture, conservation and decoded foot tests, rebuilt battle/atlas and complete final visual review.
supportedActionCandidate.visualFinding: All nine candidate techniques (36 sheets), eight four-angle Lightning Strike sheets, and all twelve enlarged source face/body slices actually inspected and passed. Front-paw toes remain above the floor and the torso moves coherently over the support paws.
supportedActionCandidate.finalVisualFinding: All 24 final source/battle face/body slices, 32 low/medium runtime slices, 36 rebuilt battle technique sheets, six fresh idle sheets and all 16 atlas cells actually inspected and passed.

supersededFailedTechniqueReview.label: independent-legendary-008-techniques-v1
supersededFailedTechniqueReview.finding: During Lightning Strike the foreground front paw loses its toes through the floor at .48 seconds; windup also drives hind feet below their support plane. Four original technique sheets and two native defect frames actually inspected. Metadata-only host ownership diagnostic retained the paw defect (two side sheets inspected) and was rejected.
